goal.source_text: Maximize this rocket fin's stability, keep drag low, keep it under 40 g, must fit a 3-inch body tube.
assumptions: The 40 g limit applies to all fins combined, since the goal does not say per fin.
The 3-inch body tube (76.2 mm diameter) is already set in the context, so no separate dimension constraint is added.
Stability is targeted at about 2.5 calibers rather than maximized, because more than about 3 calibers causes weathercocking.
Fin count is left free between 3 and 4 because the goal does not specify it.
Design velocity of 120 m/s is taken from the context since the goal does not state a speed.

message.body:
Starting from an infeasible seed (59.717 g, over the 40 g limit), the agent moved to a 3-fin, 55 mm root chord, 85 mm semi-span fin with 55 deg sweep, 0.85 taper and beveled edges. This cut fin mass to 34.924 g and drag from 2.618 N to 1.734 N while putting stability at 2.508 cal against the 2.5 target (seed 2.232). Physically, the high sweep holds the center of pressure where the target needs it, so stability comes from sweep and span rather than from thick or large-chord, heavy fins. On the same 40-evaluation budget, the agent beat random search (aggregate 0.8229 vs 0.7552) but lost to CMA-ES (0.8537), whose fin is lighter at 22.788 g with lower drag at 1.357 N and stability of 2.443 cal. CMA-ES also has a much lower flutter margin (1.65 vs 3.596 for the champion), so the agent's design may be the more conservative choice despite the lower score. Next, check the CMA-ES design's flutter margin with a higher-fidelity or structural analysis, and verify that the champion's 85 mm semi-span fits the 3-inch body tube and handling requirements.

**Caveats:** The high-fidelity check shows drag about 4% higher (1.8032 N vs 1.734 N) and CNa about 3% lower than the fast model, so the real drag advantage is slightly smaller.; The fast model's flutter margin is only an estimate, and the lower margins of the CMA-ES design (1.65) cannot be trusted without structural validation.; The fast model does not capture material, fin-can attachment or tube-fit details, so the 3-inch body tube fit and the 34.9 g mass need physical confirmation.
